characterization_methods.key_findings: M2-HR shows the presence of δ-ferrite, α-ferrite and a very fine martensitic-austenitic (α′+γ) phase; the 500 nm panel resolves a fine lath/lamellar α′+γ morphology alongside blocky δ/α-ferrite. A significantly higher amount of ferrite, especially δ-ferrite, is observed in M2 compared to M1.
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the microstructure and identify the phases present in the M2-HR (hot-rolled) sample
characterization_methods.technique: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) in secondary electron (SE) mode

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: PANalytical Empyrean instrument with Cu-Kα radiation (λ = 1.542 Å)
characterization_methods.key_findings: XRD confirms the presence of ferrite/martensite and austenite in M2-HR; the fraction of γ phase is calculated as 5.7 % for M2 steel. Reflections labelled α 110, α 200, α 211, α 220, γ 111, γ 200.
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification and determination of the austenite volume fraction in the hot-rolled M2 sample

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Tinius Olsen ST25 universal testing machine (UTM) equipped with a 25 kN load cell
characterization_methods.key_findings: M2-HR shows UTS of 1055 ± 15 MPa and total elongation of 15.4 ± 0.8 %, with a brittle fracture behaviour.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature, strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; dog-bone specimen with gauge length 2 mm, thickness 1 mm, width 1 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the tensile properties (strength and ductility) of the hot-rolled M2 sample

characterization_methods.key_findings: Observation of cleavage fracture features such as river markings (plateaus and ledges) in the fractograph of the HR sample, supporting its brittle nature.
characterization_methods.purpose: Understand the fracture behaviour of the hot-rolled M2 sample

analytical_models.equation_role: Predicts the martensite start temperature from the austenite composition at hot-rolling temperature
analytical_models.model_note: Ms(°C) = 539 - 423C - 30.4Mn - 7.5Si + 30Al. Values calculated as 319 and 296 °C for M1 and M2 respectively.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Individual elemental concentrations (C, Mn, Si, Al) taken corresponding to the austenite phase at hot-rolling temperatures, in wt.%
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The calculated Ms of 296 °C for M2-HR (319 °C for M1) indicates transformation of some austenite into martensite during cooling, supporting the observation of martensite in the M2-HR sample.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Equilibrium phase fractions as a function of temperature for the Fe–8Mn–3Al–1Si–0.2C (M2) composition; lower critical temperature taken as 600 °C considering the limited diffusion capacity of Mn at lower temperatures
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Predicts δ-ferrite as an equilibrium phase in the intercritical temperature (ICT) range for the 3Al–1Si system, consistent with the δ-ferrite observed in the M2-HR hot-rolled sample (a significantly higher amount of ferrite, especially δ-ferrite, is expected according to the thermodynamic predictions owing to the presence of Si).

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Hot-rolled M2 (M2-HR) is brittle with high UTS (1055 ± 15 MPa) and very low total elongation (15.4 ± 0.8 %), whereas the intercritically annealed condition of the same steel (M2-IA) is ductile with 698 ± 20 MPa UTS and 59.4 ± 0.6 % TE. High strength and poor elongation of the HR sample are attributed to the presence of martensite.

processing_steps.method: vacuum arc melting followed by 4× remelting (ingot flipped before each remelt)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The two steel compositions (Fe–8Mn–3Al-0.2C = M1 and Fe–8Mn–3Al–1Si-0.2C = M2) were fabricated using a vacuum arc melting furnace; the melted ingot was remelted 4 times by flipping the ingot before each remelt to ensure complete and uniform melting of the raw materials throughout the ingot.
Homogenization of as-cast samples at 1100 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching; this condition is designated M2-HQ. This is the parent process (proc_hq-1100c-2h) of proc_hr-1100-900c.

Samples were hot-rolled at 1100 °C to reduce the thickness by 50 %, with finish rolling temperatures reaching around 900 °C. δ-ferrite in M2 forms while soaking at 1100 °C before hot rolling, and some fraction of α-ferrite forms from γ during finish rolling.
Hot rolling was followed by air cooling. Martensite forms in M2 during air cooling after hot rolling (calculated Ms = 296 °C), giving the final M2-HR state.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: dog-bone shaped specimen, gauge length 2 mm, thickness 1 mm, width 1 mm (machined by wire electric discharge machining, wire-EDM)

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–strain curve of M2-HR (Fig. 10d): rises to a peak near ~1000 MPa at ~15 % strain then fractures abruptly (brittle), with very low total elongation.

phases_present.morphology: blocky / fine ferrite regions adjacent to α′+γ

very fine lath-type within the martensitic-austenitic (α′+γ) phase

structures.overall_structure: Hot-rolled M2 (Fe–8Mn–3Al–1Si–0.2C) microstructure comprising multiple phases: δ-ferrite, α-ferrite, and a very fine martensitic-austenitic (α′ + γ) phase. A significantly higher amount of ferrite, especially δ-ferrite, is present in M2 compared to the Si-free M1 steel, as expected from thermodynamic predictions owing to the presence of Si. XRD confirms the presence of ferrite/martensite and only a small austenite fraction (fγ = 5.7 %) in M2-HR.

unmapped_findings: The hot-rolled M2 sample (M2-HR) contains martensite, which formed in the steel during air cooling after hot rolling; this is supported by the calculated Ms temperature of 296 °C for M2-HR, which lies above room temperature.

The hot-rolled M2 sample shows brittle behaviour with a significantly high UTS (1055 ± 15 MPa) and very low total elongation (15.4 ± 0.8 %); its fractograph exhibits cleavage fracture features (river markings, plateaus and ledges) indicating crack propagation along parallel planes.
δ-ferrite in the M2 steel forms while soaking at 1100 °C before hot rolling, and some fraction of α-ferrite forms from γ when the steel is subjected to finish rolling temperatures around 900 °C.

Grain size distribution (Fig. 8b) reports M2 grains mostly in the ~0.25–0.5 μm bin (~92 %) with a small (~3 %) population near 1.5 μm, but this distribution is reported for the intercritically annealed samples (M2-IA), not for the M2-HR sample.
